fetch-news.mutate.sh: fetch-news.mjs was the only script in scripts/news/ with a suite and no mutation harness, and the largest surface there. Four mutations, each killing a named arm, MUTATE_EXIT=0, now running in CI. Suite 66 -> 68.

docs/DIGEST-EVAL.md §3b: the twin editions were generated over the SAME eight items, answering ADR-001's follow-up with data rather than argument.

measured_retractions.the two models do not fit on a 4 GB card: FALSE — they coexist at 3345 MB of 4096, both listed in /api/ps, nvidia-smi agreeing at 3323 MiB
measured_retractions.ollama waits for a slot rather than evic: FALSE as a rule — one run coexisted (~35 s), another evicted (4.6 s); the behaviour is not stable between runs
measured_retractions.a cold load is always ~7 s so the probe: FALSE — observed loads span 4.6 s to ~35 s, and the budget was 30 s, inside that spread

measured_established: A model being LOADED is not listed by /api/ps until it finishes — empty for 8.5 s of an 8.7 s cold load while the GPU already read 2743 MiB. So 'generation timed out AND /api/ps empty' is a load in progress, not an idle server and not a wedged runner. This closes the 20:47 attribution the previous handoff left open.

OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS=1 CLOSED as unjustified, not deferred — it fixes a behaviour that does not exist as described, needed root, and would have changed behaviour for every ollama client on this machine.
Retractions keep visible what they retract. The original GPU section sits above its correction; the refuted claim had reached four places and all four were corrected in the same change.
The suite caps NEWS_LLM_TIMEOUT_MS as a fail-fast guarantee: no arm needs the real model, and without it a mutation that let a wedged server through ran the harness past 600 s.
The entity check stays advisory. §3b makes that case stronger, not weaker — a check with a known false negative must not be the thing that clears an edition.

context_notes: One through-line, and it is the same one the previous handoff recorded from the other side: a fix that addresses one direction reads as finished, and an instrument that cannot fail reads as a pass. This session the instrument was my own reasoning. I explained the cron failure three times without reproducing it — 'wedged runner', then 'GPU standoff', then 'identifies no cause' — and each was written into code, tests and docs before the next one refuted it. What finally settled it was loading a model while polling /api/ps every 0.4 s: the list is empty for the whole load. Two claims this repo had carried as measured fact fell in the same experiment, including one I had documented FURTHER earlier in the same session. Secondary instances, all caught by controls rather than by care: a suite read 59 assertions instead of 66 because I had switched to main; a grep for 'LOAD IN PROGRESS' returned 0 because the string is 'LOAD IS IN PROGRESS'; a production smoke returned 000 for three URLs including the control because I invented the hostname; a three-arm crontab measurement returned three identical failures because the -T flag does not exist here. In every one, the zero looked like a finding and was a blind instrument. The rule that earned its keep: print the positive control beside the zero, in the same run.
